text.p: The mark suffered a bruising day on its European crosses, falling nearly seven lire against the Italian currency after German Chancellor Helmut Kohl said that Germany and Italy wanted to stick to the planned timetable for monetary union.
The mark has suffered from all sides, analysts said, with pressure from Germany's record unemployment levels, a surging dollar and renewed enthousiasm for a broadly based EMU.
After dropping sharply in early morning trade, the mark clawed its way back in Europe before being sent into a tailspin, hitting fresh 32-month lows against the dollar.
